evidence: In the same chunk, Table 26-1 rows are 'Inference Sharding', 'Semantic Response Cache', and 'Circuit Breaker'; Table 26-2 rows are 'GPU Shard', 'Semantic Response Cache', 'Circuit Breaker', and 'Cost'. No row or column addresses task quality, quantized memory/workspace, rollback, or quantization-specific SLO verification.

quoted_clause: Hybrid-attention models cut it ~4–14× at the mechanism in the named configurations — from GLM's 4.4× normalized per-layer KV measure to DeepSeek's ~7%-of-V3.2 single-token KV (≈14×) — different scopes (per-layer normalized vs single-token KV at 1M context), not directly comparable — a band across models, not a universal constant
observed: The sentence uses 'it' to refer to the canonical KV constant, but the cited 4.4× and ~14× are vendor-relative reductions (GLM vs GLM-5.3 per-layer normalized; DeepSeek V4 vs V3.2 single-token KV), not reductions of the canonical 70B full-MHA constant. The text also says the scopes are not directly comparable, so they cannot form a single band of reductions to the canonical constant.
evidence: Earlier in the same section: 'Each row is a model's vendor-reported ratio of its own stated reference ... they do not share a common denominator, so they must not be read as percentages of a single baseline. The canonical 70B dense full-MHA model is the book's foundational teaching model, not the denominator for these percentages.'
root_cause: Compressing vendor-relative, scope-different ratios into a single 'cut it 4–14×' phrase reintroduces the common-denominator reading the paragraph warns against.
correction: Replace with: 'The named models report KV reductions of 4.4× to ~14× relative to their own vendor-stated references; these are not reductions of the canonical full-MHA constant, and the two cited ratios are not directly comparable to one another because their scopes differ.'
acceptance_test: No sentence implies that the 4.4× and ~14× values share a common denominator or directly reduce the canonical 2.62/1.31 MB/token constants; all vendor-relative ratios are explicitly scoped to their own references.

quoted_clause: alerts fire when a FACT crosses its safety threshold or when a DERIVED quantity — throughput per shard, cost per query, fleet-wide rps — crosses a boundary (e.g., the p99 TTFT SLO, the fallback-rate target < 10% of Table 26-2, or the queue-depth limits of Ch 15)

quoted_clause: lower engine load cannot raise SM utilization
observed: The statement is too absolute. Under the assumed unchanged request mix and per-request service time, lower engine load should not raise average SM utilization, but in general a lower aggregate load can have higher SM utilization if the mix shifts toward more compute-bound prefill or different batch composition.
evidence: The same note says the scaling 'assumes per-request service time is unchanged between the two load points'; that assumption is not present in the quoted clause.
root_cause: A mechanism-level caveat was compressed into a universal 'cannot'.
correction: Reword: 'under the assumed unchanged per-request service time and request mix, lower engine load should not raise average SM utilization; a load test must measure both under one definition.'
acceptance_test: No unqualified 'cannot' claim about SM utilization and load appears; the statement is scoped to the worked-example assumptions.

quoted_clause: architecture alone never tells an architect how good a frontier model is

evidence: The same section says architecture is 'one ingredient' and that post-training/runtime may carry much of the gap, not that architecture provides no information.
root_cause: Rhetorical emphasis overstates the evidentiary point.
correction: Use 'architecture alone does not determine how good a frontier model is' or 'architecture alone is not a reliable indicator of how good...'
acceptance_test: The sentence no longer uses an unqualified universal; it matches the interpretation that architecture is necessary but not sufficient.

evidence: The same paragraph defines the SLO as 'p99 ≤ 800 ms TTFT' and then describes a per-request timeout. Treating the p99 quantile itself as a per-request deadline conflates distribution-level SLO with request-level deadline.
